observations: Photo 0: a heap of used car engine and gearbox mounts on wooden shelves, a dealer's stock display with a watermark.
Mixed types: round rubber bushing mounts, bracket mounts with studs, several heavily rusted steel brackets.
One mount has handwritten white marker text on it that looks like a buyer's or seller's name, not a part number.
No part numbers, vehicle make, or OEM stamps are readable.
Quantity on offer and which piece is for sale are not stated; rubber condition (cracks, oil soaking) cannot be judged at this distance.

claims.claim: For engine seating and engine mounting
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows rubber and steel engine and gearbox mounts.

risks.risk: Vehicle fitment unknown; a mount for the wrong car is worthless to the buyer
risks.proof: Close photo of the part number stamped on the chosen mount, or the car make, model and year it came off
risks.if_unproven: as a single generic used mount of unknown fitment

risks.risk: Rubber may be cracked, torn, collapsed or oil soaked; hydraulic mounts may be leaking
risks.proof: Close photo of each side of the rubber, plus a clip of flexing it by hand
risks.if_unproven: as worn, near end of life

risks.risk: Quantity offered is unclear; the photo is a shop heap
risks.proof: Photo of the exact pieces on offer laid out and counted with a handwritten code in shot

risks.risk: Heavy rust on brackets may hide cracks or thinned metal
risks.proof: Close photo of the bracket and bolt holes on the chosen piece

proof_requests: Car make, model and year, or the part number on the exact mount offered
Photo of the exact pieces on offer, counted, with a handwritten code in shot
Close photos of the rubber on each piece
response.reason: These are plainly used engine mounts, a plain good identified by type, so they can be priced at the worst case as one used mount of unknown fitment in worn condition until the fitment and quantity are shown.
